A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DUT research work, with complete 19-page main texts, references and Appendices A–M. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original rendering and geometry evaluations, component ablations, runtime measurements and appendix robustness experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and reports revised runtime measurements for the larger model variant.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same double texture unprojection, GeoNet deformation prediction, GauNet appearance prediction, Gaussian scale refinement and training losses.

E1.justification: Both versions use DynaCap, ASH, THUman4.0 and the collected subject. The appendix scenarios involving OOD motions, mocap errors, loose clothing and hair, novel lighting and topology changes are retained.

E2.justification: Rendering comparisons retain ENeRF, DVA, HoloChar and GHG; geometry comparisons retain DDC and LBS. Comparator membership in the corresponding appendix comparisons is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Splits, metrics, training schedules and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Table 4 retains the same GPUs and texture/rendering resolutions; its revised timings do not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: Appendix F revises the stage-by-stage timing evidence in its existing runtime ablation for the 512-texture variant across GPUs and rendering resolutions. The questions tested and all other component ablations, robustness tests and case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions average runtime over 100 frames and repeat that process three times. The OOD standard-deviation reporting and other statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Under unchanged reported settings, Table 4 revises 512-texture FPS from 33.91/34.04 to 26.92/26.95 on RTX3090 at 1K/4K, and from 47.59/47.61 to 45.93/46.73 on H100. Corresponding cumulative stage timings change. Figure 1 updates the RTX3090 points, and Appendix F changes the runtime bound from 30 to 38 ms. Other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, definitions and loss expressions in Equations 1–26 are unchanged, including the appendix visibility and loss details.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about real-time rendering, image-conditioned geometry, rendering quality and generalization.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, the quality–speed tradeoff and stated limitations are unchanged. Appendix F's revised numerical runtime bound changes a reported result without adding a new interpretation.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, hardware, training schedules, baseline reproduction details and project access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and positioning relative to prior geometry and sparse-view rendering methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Apart from the localized runtime-number substitution, prose, terminology, section ordering and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1's two speed–quality plots are redrawn with repositioned Ours-Large markers and labels. Other figures, table structures, captions and page organization are retained.

improvement.justification: Figure 1, Table 4 and Appendix F consistently report revised, slower Ours-Large timings, but v3 does not explain why the measurements changed. Both versions are internally consistent in these displays, and the remaining scientific content is unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the revisions improve measurement accuracy, preventing a reliable judgment of net paper quality.
